newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - PGMs unpredictable, gold eyes support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - PGMs unpredictable, gold eyes support.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Platinum and palladium have potential for extreme volatility as long as market tightness persists, analysts said. Platinum will meet resistance at $435.
Vulnerable gold has found some support at $340 for now amid flattening near-term indicators.

PLATINUM/PALLADIUM - The extreme tightness in the palladium market continues and prices are subject to further volatility, dealers and analysts said. One-month lease rates were cited at around 165 percent, close to Wednesday's highs.
But traders reported an eerie lull in trading as the dazed market took stock of the situation.
"This morning it's not so frantic as last night because of the wide spread. People are not prepared to trade and everyone is waiting for news," traders said.
The market was anxiously awaiting fresh developments in talks between Russian exporters and Japanese consumers regarding long-delayed Russian supplies.
Palladium was last indicated at $228/$238, near Wednesday's highs.
Platinum was is a similar situation to palladium.
Chartwise, dealers said the $435 resistance level from February 1995 could temporarily cap the market.
It was last indicated at $430/$440, up about $4 from Wednesday's close.
GOLD - The market is being snubbed as all eyes turn to the platinum group metals (PGMs), and prices have failed to break out of a $340-$347 range despite volatility in the white metals.
"Gold and silver are basically a non-event," a dealer said.
Bullion came under pressure on Wednesday on bearishly construed developments in German plans to revalue gold reserves.
For the time being the $340 area was holding steady, although analysts suspected it would be breached in due course.
"There was some support below $341 but expect this to be breached, as we remain focused on $339.50 (the year's low)," brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary referring to Comex June futures.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was indicated at $341.25/$341.75, versus the New York close of $341.00/$341.50.
SILVER - Like gold silver is trading in a tight range within a broader $4.60-$4.85 band.
It was last indicated at $4.72/$4.74, unchanged from Wednesday's new York close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
